newsitem.title: USA: Virginia municipalities buy industrial park site.
newsitem.headline: Virginia municipalities buy industrial park site.

text.p: Virginia's Rockbridge County and cities of Lexington and Buena Vista agreed to buy land for an industrial park, becoming the first municipalities to use the state's new industrial development law.
Richmond Times-Dispatch said the deal was signed Tuesday and was related to the purchase by Des Champs Laboratories Inc of property formerly owned by the Blue Bird Bus Co.

Des Champ, which makes air-to-air heat exchangers and energy saving systems, agreed to buy a vacant manufacutring building at the Blue Bird site plus 30 surrounding acres for $1.85 million, the newspaper said.

The three-government partnership will buy the remaining 46 acres at the site for $800,000, building an industrial park and sharing tax revenues from incoming businesses. They will also share tax revenues from the Des Champ facility, which is expected to hire 200 workers within two months.
The agreement was made possible by the General Assembly's decision last year to allow municipalities to form regional indsutrial development authorities and split the revenue.
Rockbridge County paid 55 percent of the land cost, Buena Vista 30 percent and Lexington 15 percent. They will share the revenues on a pro-rated basis.
